title: India's cotton imports to surge 3.5-fold, output revised up: CAI
content:
The Cotton Association of India (CAI) has raised its 2025-26 cotton crop estimate to 337 lakh bales and increased domestic consumption to 348 lakh bales.
Cotton imports are now projected to surge 362 per cent to 60 lakh bales, while exports are expected to decline to 15 lakh bales.
Closing stocks are estimated at 89.59 lakh bales, significantly higher than last season.

title: ICE cotton falls further as broader commodity weakness weighs
content:
ICE cotton futures fell for a second straight session, with the December 2026 contract slipping below the key 80-cent level as broad commodity weakness, a stronger US dollar and profit-taking outweighed supportive cotton fundamentals.
Strong Chinese demand and tight ICE stocks remained supportive, but thin trading and macroeconomic concerns kept prices under pressure.

title: China's apparel profits fall 28% as textile profits rise 16.6%
content:
China’s textile profits rose 16.6 per cent in January–June 2026, while apparel profits fell 28 per cent, widening the mill-factory gap.
TexPro data show fibre, yarn and fabric exports rose 1.3 per cent to $41.96 billion in January–May, but apparel exports fell 1.95 per cent to $54.85 billion.
Sourcing teams may cut China sewing exposure yet still rely on Chinese inputs across Asian garment hubs.

title: Vietnamese city aims raising direct exim throughput above 80% by 2030
content:
Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City aims at raising the proportion of imports and exports handled directly through its seaports, airports, railway terminals and ICDs to over 80 per cent by 2030 to reduce logistics costs, enhance competitiveness and back sustainable growth in external trade.
It has set an average annual export growth target of 10-11 per cent and import growth target of 9-10 per cent over the period.

title: India's cotton duty waiver reshapes sourcing before July 31
content:
India's 11 per cent raw cotton import-duty waiver is cutting landed costs for mills while domestic supply remains tight.
US Section 301 tariffs now apply to most Indian goods, but the waiver helps spinners manage input costs rather than export duties.
CCI procurement is due to close on July 31, with the waiver set to expire on October 31, shaping buying windows.

title: Indonesia's fabric imports rise 5% in Jan-Apr, prices also up
content:
Indonesia's fabric imports rose 4.9 per cent year on year to $1.481 billion in January-April 2026, with volumes at 220.81 million kg.
The average import price increased to $6.71 per kg, above 2025 and 2024 levels, signalling demand for higher-value inputs.
China held 56.46 per cent share, while Vietnam's shipments grew 26.9 per cent, affecting sourcing choices for mills and apparel exporters.

title: India's Snitch acquires Berrylush, enters women's fashion
content:
Snitch has acquired women’s western-wear label Berrylush, marking its move into women’s fashion beyond menswear.
Berrylush will retain its identity while using Snitch’s product, technology, supply chain, marketing and omnichannel retail capabilities.

title: US tariff threatens Nigerian exports, may reduce forex earnings: SEREC
content:
The US decision to impose a 12.5-per cent tariff on Nigerian exports could undermine the country’s non-oil export drive, reduce foreign exchange earnings and further expose the fragility of the nation’s economy if urgent countermeasures are not taken, a research centre in Lagos has cautioned. 
Sectors identified as most vulnerable to the new tariff include leather products and manufactured consumer goods.

title: India sustains growth momentum during Q1 FY27: Finance Ministry
content:
Despite heightened global uncertainty, the Indian economy sustained growth momentum during Q1 FY27, according to Monthly Economic Review for July by the department of economic affairs. 
Industrial activity improved during Q1 FY27. 
In manufacturing, growth moderated sequentially due to slower growth in new orders and output, and cautious business sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainties.

title: Bangladesh PM seeks solutions to textile gas crisis
content:
Bangladesh has set a high-level inter-ministerial committee to prepare swift remedies for textile-sector bottlenecks, including gas shortages disrupting production.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has asked for another meeting within a week to finalise practical steps.
BTMA raised energy shortages, higher production costs and operational issues affecting export competitiveness.

title: US cotton quota faces Brazil's cost edge in Asia
content:
US Section 301 duties add a cotton tariff-rate quota for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia garments made with US-origin fibre.
US cotton still lands in Asia about five cents per pound above Brazilian bales, limiting the duty benefit for mills and sourcing teams.
Pending verification rules will decide whether the quota shifts fibre buying or mainly reshapes export documentation.

title: India-EU FTA sets CBAM framework for MSME exporters
content:
India-EU FTA text includes a dedicated CBAM annexure with a work plan for flexibility, compliance and carbon-price engagement.
The framework matters for MSME exporters facing EU verification and embedded-carbon reporting requirements.
The commerce ministry plans district-level and electronic outreach before the pact is signed later this year.

title: Barmag launches 6020 ceramic oiler for low-titer polyamide yarns
content:
Barmag’s new 6020 ceramic oiler targets PA6 and PA6.6 low-titer yarns (5–100 denier), improving spinfinish application, yarn quality and process stability. 
The integrated ceramic shaft and optimised yarn guidance reduce spray-off, contamination and filament damage. 
Customer trials showed spray-off-free processing and around 23 per cent higher spinfinish application than conventional solutions.

title: Germany's Adidas posts record Q2 revenue, raises FY26 sales outlook
content:
Adidas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of €6.7 billion (~$8.90 billion), up 13 per cent year on year, driven by strong direct-to-consumer growth, robust apparel demand and FIFA World Cup momentum. 
Operating profit rose to €574 million, while DTC sales increased 25 per cent. 
The company raised its full-year revenue growth forecast to 9–10 per cent despite tariff and sourcing cost pressures.

title: Germany's Adidas appoints Birgit Kretschmer as next CFO
content:
adidas has appointed Birgit Kretschmer to its Executive Board from September 1, 2026, to succeed Harm Ohlmeyer as chief financial officer (CFO) at year-end after he opted not to extend his mandate.
Kretschmer returns with 25 years at adidas and six as C&A’s CFO, giving the sportswear group finance, vertical retail and operational control experience as Ohlmeyer supports the transition.

title: Jack orders 2,000 humanoid robots, testing apparel’s labour model
content:
Jack Technology has ordered 2,000 humanoid robots with Siemens to automate difficult sewing tasks, but pilots do not yet show full-line autonomy. 
If performance scales across fabrics and styles, robotics could weaken wage-cost advantages in Bangladesh, Cambodia and Ethiopia. 
Sourcing teams will track payback, throughput, defects, rival machinery moves and industry responses to judge adoption.

title: Vietnam promotes VIS 2026 in Beijing to strengthen trade ties
content:
Vietnam's Trade Office in China promoted Vietnam International Sourcing (VIS) 2026 at a Beijing conference on July 28 to strengthen trade ties and attract global buyers. 
The September event in Ho Chi Minh City will connect Vietnamese exporters with international buyers.
Chinese businesses, retailers, importers and e-commerce firms expressed strong interest in attending and forming long-term partnerships.

title: Tariff gaps turn multi-country platforms into apparel’s new edge
content:
PDS and Indonesia’s Busana have formed a six-country apparel sourcing partnership spanning Asia, Central America and Italy.
The model lets brands shift orders as tariffs, costs, capacity and delivery needs change, reducing reliance on single-country suppliers.
US buyers are increasing CAFTA-DR sourcing and favouring strategic vendor consolidation.

title: Bangladesh garment bodies seek temporary CNG relief from govt
content:
Two garment trade bodies in Bangladesh have called for temporarily allowing export units to collect CNG in cylinders from filling stations to keep production running.
The request follows an acute gas shortage after the shutdown of a floating LNG terminal at Moheshkhali and Titas instructing filling stations to stop selling CNG in open cylinders or gas cascade cylinders not mounted on authorised vehicles.
